Evaluate model performance across resamples or time windows

Source: R/model_performance_bootstrap_rmse.R
validate_performance.Rd

Refit a pricing model and score its predictions across resamples or time windows. By default, the model is fitted and scored on the same bootstrap sample. Evaluation on rows outside that fit depends on the sampling design.

Usage

validate_performance(
  model,
  data,
  n_resamples = 50,
  sample_fraction = 1,
  metric = "rmse",
  sampling = c("bootstrap", "split"),
  show_progress = TRUE,
  rmse_model = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  frac = NULL,
  metrics = "rmse",
  method = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  initial = NULL,
  horizon = 1
)

Arguments

model

A fitted model object that can be updated on resampled data.

data

Data frame containing the model response and predictors.

n_resamples

Positive whole number. Number of resampling replicates. Default is 50.

sample_fraction

Fraction of input rows to draw for each random training sample, before adding any rows for missing factor levels. Must be in (0, 1]. Default is 1. Not used for rolling validation.

metric

Legacy argument that accepts only "rmse". Use metrics to select metrics.

sampling

Character string. Use "bootstrap" (default) to sample training rows with replacement, "split" to sample without replacement, or "rolling" for expanding-window temporal validation.

show_progress

Logical. Show a progress bar during resampling. Default is TRUE.

rmse_model

Optional finite numeric RMSE for the original fitted model. If NULL and RMSE is selected, it is calculated from model and data.

n, frac

Deprecated argument names. Use n_resamples and sample_fraction instead.

metrics

Character vector of distinct metrics in the desired output order: "rmse" (default), "mae", or "deviance".

method

Alternative name for sampling. Supply only one of the two.

time

For rolling validation, name of a column containing numeric periods, dates, date-times or an ordered factor. Missing periods are not allowed.

initial

For rolling validation, number of distinct periods in the first training window.

horizon

For rolling validation, number of subsequent distinct periods evaluated at each origin. Default is 1.

Value

For rolling validation, a data frame with one row per origin: iteration, train_start, train_end, test_start, test_end, n_train, n_test and the requested metric columns. Counts refer to the input rows in each window. Scores are calculated on the test rows; binomial prediction errors use proportions for grouped responses.

For random resampling, a list of class "bootstrap_performance". For RMSE alone, the original structure is unchanged: rmse_bs contains the scores, rmse_mod contains the original model's RMSE, and metric, sampling, n_resamples, sample_fraction, n and frac describe the run. When another metric is selected, scores is a data frame with one row per replicate and a column for each requested metric, and original_scores is a named numeric vector for the original model on data. metric records the selected metric names; rmse_bs and rmse_mod are NULL if RMSE was not selected. For these results, as.vector() returns scores for the first requested metric.

Details

Resampling design

DesignTraining rowsEvaluation rows
Bootstrap, fraction 1Full-size draw with replacementSame sample (in sample)
Bootstrap, fraction < 1Draw with replacementOut-of-bag rows
Split, fraction < 1Draw without replacementRemaining rows
Split, fraction 1All input rowsSame rows (in sample)
RollingExpanding windowSubsequent periods

In a bootstrap, sample_fraction = 0.8 means 80 draws per 100 input rows, with replacement. Some rows can be drawn more than once, so the out-of-bag set is not a fixed 20% of the data.

For random resampling, factor levels come from the supplied data. For factor columns used directly in the model, rows may be added to the training sample to cover levels that were not drawn. These rows are then excluded from held-out evaluation. If no evaluation rows remain, try a smaller sample_fraction.

Rolling-origin validation

With sampling = "rolling", fit the GLM to the earliest initial periods, score the next horizon periods, then advance the origin by one observed period at a time. Training and test periods never overlap within a window, but test windows can overlap across origins when horizon > 1. The number of windows follows from the available periods, not n_resamples or sample_fraction.

Supply an unrestricted stats::glm() as the model specification. It is fitted on each training window. Transformations such as scale() learn their parameters from the training rows. Precomputed predictors must not use future data. Supply weights and offsets using columns in data, and filter any intended subset before calling the function. Observation-level starting values are not supported. A factor level unseen in training produces an error; future observations are not added to the training window.

Rolling validation assesses a specification repeatedly fitted to history. For temporal calibration of one fixed fitted model, use calibration_analysis() with by set to the period column.

Metrics and interpretation

RMSE (root mean squared error) and MAE (mean absolute error) are unweighted summaries of response-scale errors. For an exposure-offset Poisson model these are errors in claim counts, not claim frequency per unit exposure. For a binomial GLM, the errors are on the probability scale: two-column responses are converted to proportions, and factor responses use the fitted model's reference level to define zero. Predictive deviance sums the fitted GLM family's deviance contributions on the evaluation rows, using those rows' response-scale predictions (including offsets) and observation weights. Specify weights and offsets using columns in data, rather than separate row-aligned vectors, so the model can be refitted and evaluated on each sample. Total deviance can vary with the number and weight of evaluation rows as well as with prediction quality. On the original estimation rows with the same predictions and weights, it agrees with the residual deviance reported by model_performance().

Under random resampling, the score distribution reflects variation in both the refitted models and the rows used to score them. It does not isolate coefficient stability; use coefficient_stability() for that. Even with held-out rows, resampling the observed portfolio is not independent validation on a future or external portfolio.

See also

rmse(), model_performance(), autoplot.bootstrap_performance()

Author

Martin Haringa

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
mod1 <- glm(nclaims ~ age_policyholder, data = MTPL,
            offset = log(exposure), family = poisson())

# Draw with replacement and score on the resampled training rows.
x <- validate_performance(mod1, MTPL, n_resamples = 80,
                          show_progress = FALSE)
print(x)
autoplot(x)

# Draw 80% of the rows without replacement; score on the held-out rows.
x_frac <- validate_performance(mod1, MTPL, n_resamples = 50,
                               sample_fraction = .8, sampling = "split",
                               show_progress = FALSE,
                               metrics = c("rmse", "mae", "deviance"))
head(x_frac$scores)
autoplot(x_frac, metric = "rmse")
} # }

# Illustrative years; MTPL2 does not contain real policy dates.
portfolio <- as.data.frame(MTPL2)
portfolio$year <- rep(2020:2025, length.out = nrow(portfolio))
model <- glm(nclaims ~ factor(area) + offset(log(exposure)),
             family = poisson(), data = portfolio)
validate_performance(
  model, portfolio, sampling = "rolling", time = "year", initial = 3,
  metrics = c("rmse", "mae", "deviance"), show_progress = FALSE
)
#>   iteration train_start train_end test_start test_end n_train n_test      rmse
#> 1         1        2020      2022       2023     2023    1500    500 0.3148918
#> 2         2        2020      2023       2024     2024    2000    500 0.3402196
#> 3         3        2020      2024       2025     2025    2500    500 0.3490226
#>         mae deviance
#> 1 0.2056950 237.7274
#> 2 0.2084982 259.1681
#> 3 0.2086374 255.4882
